simple.meaning: אֲזִקִּים (ʼăziqqîym) is a Hebrew word meaning “manacles.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֲזִקִּים (H246) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Jeremiah 40:1, with occurrences in Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲזִקִּים (H246) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֲזִקִּים (H246) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֲזִקִּים (ʼăziqqîym) / H246 is traced through Jeremiah 40:1, Jeremiah 40:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah, who were carried away captive to Babylon.

majorEvents.label: Movement or place
majorEvents.evidenceText: Now, behold, I release you today from the chains which are on your hand. If it seems good to you to come with me into Babylon, come, and I will take care of you; but if it seems bad to you to come with me into Babylon, don’t. Behold, all the land is before you. Where it seems good and right to you to go, there go.”
